intro: The n-Deklination is the one group of nouns that changes its ending for case, and it gets its own quiz here (the adjective-nouns such as der Angestellte had theirs in the previous module). A group of masculine nouns add -n or -en in every case except the nominative singular: der Student → den Studenten, dem Studenten, des Studenten, die Studenten. The members are predictable: (1) masculine nouns for people and animals ending in -e: der Kollege, der Kunde, der Junge, der Neffe, der Löwe, der Affe; (2) masculine nouns with foreign endings -ent, -ant, -ist, -at, -oge, -graf, -nom: der Student, der Praktikant, der Polizist, der Soldat, der Biologe, der Fotograf; (3) a short list of old words: der Herr (den Herrn, but die Herren), der Mensch, der Nachbar, der Bauer, der Held, der Prinz; (4) a few that also take a genitive -s: der Name (des Namens), der Gedanke (des Gedankens), das Herz (des Herzens). Missing the -n on 'mit dem Kollegen' or 'an Herrn Müller' is a small error that every reader of your e-mail will notice.
tips[0].title: -(e)n in Akk, Dat, Gen and all plural forms
tips[0].text: der Student → den Studenten, dem Studenten, des Studenten, die Studenten. der Junge → den Jungen, dem Jungen, des Jungen, die Jungen. Only the nominative singular is bare.
tips[0].trap: English nouns don't change for case, so 'dem Student' feels complete. It isn't: dem Studenten.
tips[0].check.why: Kollege is an n-noun: every form except the nominative singular takes -n, so dative dem Kollegen.
tips[0].visual.caption: Only the nominative singular has no -n.

tips[1].title: Who belongs: -e people/animals, -ent/-ant/-ist/-at, and the old list
tips[1].text: Kollege, Kunde, Junge, Neffe, Franzose, Löwe, Affe, Hase · Student, Präsident, Praktikant, Elefant, Polizist, Tourist, Journalist, Soldat, Automat, Biologe, Fotograf · Herr, Mensch, Nachbar, Bauer, Held, Prinz, Graf, Bär. All masculine.
tips[1].check.why: Polizist (-ist) belongs to the n-group and takes -en; Lehrer is an ordinary noun and stays unchanged in the accusative singular.
tips[2].title: Herr, Name, Herz — the odd ones
tips[2].text: der Herr → den Herrn, dem Herrn, des Herrn — but plural die Herren. der Name → den Namen, des Namens (extra -s). das Herz → dem Herzen, des Herzens (neuter, but n-declined).
tips[2].check.why: an + accusative, and Herr takes -n in the singular: an Herrn Schulz. Herren is the plural.
tips[3].title: der Kunde ist König, but den Kunden bedient man
tips[3].text: The customer is king (nominative, bare). One serves the customer (accusative, -n). Whenever the noun isn't the subject, it grows an -n.
tips[3].check.why: The customer is the object here, not the subject, so Kunde grows an -n: den Kunden.
remember[0]: Masculine + (-e person/animal, -ent/-ist/-ant/-at, Herr/Mensch/Nachbar): -n everywhere but Nom. Sg.
remember[1]: Herrn (Sg.) / Herren (Pl.); des Namens, des Herzens.
